digest.component_or_area: LLM verdict signing and provider attribution
propositions: Signed verdicts record only a model string and cannot distinguish whether the model was resolved through Bedrock, Anthropic, Ollama, or another opaque gateway, making verdicts ambiguous across first-class and best-effort tiers.

A new additive-only provider_provenance object must be stamped into verdicts to record provider name, model, endpoint host, effective tier, and capabilities, enabling consumers to validate tier-appropriate verdicts while maintaining backward compatibility.

The runner already holds all required data (resolved model, provider name, capability record, base_url) in a single scope and must assemble provenance once and reuse it rather than recomputing capabilities, to prevent divergence from the record that actually drove the run.

Credential material (userinfo from base_url or api_key) must never appear in the persisted sidecar payload; endpoint_host must be extracted via urlparse().hostname, not .netloc, to strip embedded credentials.

Verdicts must carry provenance through all three gate sidecars (plan-review, completion, code-review) and into their signed manifests, threaded from the runner result via the orchestrator/finalize_verdict functions.
Legacy payloads lacking the provider_provenance key must remain loadable and their signatures must still verify, enforcing backward compatibility for the additive change.
